## 1 · GitHub settings — no keys, five minutes

### 1.1 Publish `main` and the v1.0 release · **[BLOCKED — needs you]** · WP-01

I have prepared the merge on a branch. You need to allow `main` to move and create the release.

```bash
git checkout main
git merge --no-ff dev -m "release v1.0: full system, benchmarks and the public site"
git tag -a v1.0 -m "Gate 8: full system + benchmarks + public site"
git push origin main --tags
```

Then: **GitHub → the repo → Releases → Draft a new release → tag `v1.0`** → title `v1.0` → paste
`docs/RELEASE_v1.0.md` as the body → attach the four archives in `dist/` → Publish.

Then: **Settings → General → Default branch → `main`**.

*Why it matters:* a visitor lands on `dev`, sees no release and no license, and concludes the
project is unfinished. It is the cheapest credibility fix in this document.

*How I verify:* `git ls-remote --tags origin` shows `v1.0`, and the repo's landing page shows a
release.

### 1.2 Branch protection on `dev` · **[BLOCKED — needs you]** · WP-01, closes D-069

**Settings → Branches → Add branch ruleset** (or *Add rule*) for `dev`:

- Require a pull request before merging
- Require status checks to pass → select **`tests`** and **`web`** (they appear in the list once
  each workflow has run at least once — both have)

*Why it matters:* GIT_RULES §6 makes PR review the contribution record. Without required checks a
red build can still merge.

*How I verify:* I open a PR with a deliberately failing test and confirm merge is blocked.

### 1.3 GitHub social preview · Optional · WP-12

**Settings → General → Social preview → Upload** the 1280×640 image I generate in WP-12.

### 2.2 Hugging Face account + write token · **[BLOCKED — needs you]** · WP-04

1. <https://huggingface.co> → **Sign up** (free)
2. **Settings → Access Tokens → New token** → name `control-tower-deploy`, role **Write** → copy
3. Paste into `.env` as `HF_TOKEN=hf_...` — `.env` is gitignored; never commit it
4. **New → Space** → name `agentic-control-tower-api` → SDK **Docker** → Hardware **CPU basic
   (free)** → Public

Then add the Space secrets (**Space → Settings → Variables and secrets → New secret**):

| Secret | Value |
|---|---|
| `TMS_API_KEY` | the 32-character string from §2.3 below |
| `GEMINI_API_KEY` | the key already in your `.env` |

*Why it matters:* WP-04 is the only thing standing between the four live pages (Predict, Alerts,
Agents, Assistant) and working in production. They are built and currently show recorded evidence.

*How I verify:* `curl https://<space>.hf.space/health` returns 200, and a POST to a TMS route
without the key returns 401.

### 2.3 Regenerate `TMS_API_KEY` · **[BLOCKED — needs you]** · WP-04

The current value in `.env` is 13 characters, which was fine as a local dev placeholder and is not
fine once it is the only thing standing between the internet and the TMS write routes (D-064).

```bash
python -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))"
```

Put the result in `.env` as `TMS_API_KEY=` **and** as a Space secret of the same name.

### 2.4 LLM API key · **DONE** · WP-02, WP-07

`GEMINI_API_KEY` is already set in `.env` (53 characters) with `LLM_PROVIDER=gemini`.

Two notes:

- **There is a mismatch to settle.** `.env.example` and your `.env` say `LLM_MODEL=gemini-3.6-flash`;
  `src/common/config.py` defaults to `gemini-2.0-flash`. The `.env` value wins at runtime, so the
  behaviour is whatever `.env` says — but the two files disagree and one of them is wrong. I will
  align them in WP-01 and log which model actually answered.
- **The free tier's daily cap is the binding constraint on this project** (`docs/cost.md`). Limits
  change; check the current table at <https://ai.google.dev/pricing> before planning an evaluation
  run. Nothing in WP-01 to WP-05 needs a single call — every agent runs with `--no-llm`.

*Optional backup:* Groq (<https://console.groq.com> → API Keys, free, Llama 3.x, generous
per-minute limits). Add as `GROQ_API_KEY` and set `LLM_PROVIDER=groq` if Gemini's daily cap blocks
an evaluation.

### 2.5 Telegram bot · **[BLOCKED — needs you]** · WP-06, closes G-07

This closes the caveat the README has carried since Week 5: *no real alert has ever been sent.*

1. Telegram → search **@BotFather** → `/newbot` → follow prompts → copy the token
2. Send your new bot any message (a bot cannot start a conversation)
3. Open `https://api.telegram.org/bot<TOKEN>/getUpdates` in a browser → read `result[0].message.chat.id`
4. `.env`: `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=...` and `TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID=...`; add both as Space secrets

*How I verify:* I run the alert bot against a replay, one real message arrives in your chat, and I
save the API response to `benchmarks/raw/f2_alert_channel_live.json`. The README caveat is then
removed rather than reworded.

### 2.9 Map tiles · **DONE, no key needed** · WP-03

The map uses CARTO's publicly served basemap styles, which require no API key. That was deliberate:
a key would have to be committed into a public bundle (D-062), and the arcs are a deck.gl overlay
rather than part of the style, so tiles failing degrades the map to arcs on a blank ground rather
than to nothing. **No MapTiler account is needed.**

## 3 · Human time, not keys

These cannot be automated and they are the ones most likely to slip.

| # | What | Who | Time | Package | Why it cannot be faked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3.1 | Review 40 random adversarial evaluation cases and confirm the ground-truth labels | Lahari | half a day | WP-02 | The builder must not also be the judge — that separation is why the agent scores mean anything |
| 3.2 | Label 150 ambiguous order emails as ask / infer / refuse | you + Lahari, ~2 h each | 2 h × 2 | WP-07 | Inter-annotator agreement is the measurement; one labeller gives no agreement statistic |
| 3.3 | Two-minute user test with **three people who have never seen the project** | three classmates | 2 min each | WP-05 | The acceptance test is whether a stranger can answer "what does this do", "which lane is worst", "what does an agent do". Your opinion cannot substitute |
| 3.4 | Photograph 10 real receipts or invoices on a phone — skewed, shadowed, creased | you | 15 min | WP-08 | 97.9% on documents your own generator produced measures the generator. The gap to real documents is the finding |
| 3.5 | Record the two-minute demo video with voice on the production URL | you | half a day | WP-12 | Most people who open a CV link watch rather than read |
| 3.6 | Rehearse the demo twice in front of a person | team | 1 h | v4.0 Gate F2 | The one Gate 8 item no automation replaces |

I will generate the labelling sheet for 3.2 and the exact narration with click-by-click timings for
3.5, so both are fill-in rather than design.

## 4 · Rules for keys

- Keys live in **`.env`** locally and in **Hugging Face Space secrets** for the API. Never in
  Vercel, never in `web/`, never in a commit, a PR, a screenshot or a chat message.
- The web build is secret-free by construction (D-062) and CI greps the built bundle for Google,
  OpenAI and GitHub token patterns on every push.
- If a key ever does reach a commit: **rotate it** — do not force-push to hide it (GIT_RULES §7,
  §11) — and add a `P-` entry to `docs/problems.md`.
- Every key here is for this project only. Rotate them after the demo.
- If a free tier changes its limits, tell me the new number and I will update `docs/cost.md` and the
  server-side caps. Do not raise a cap to make a demo work — the `--no-llm` fallbacks exist for that.
